title: Proper and smooth morphisms are stable under base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X'=X\times_SS'$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $f':X'\to S'$ be its second projection, the base change of $f$ along $g$ [def-pc-base-change]. (1) If $f$ is proper (separated, of finite type and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]), then $f'$ is proper. (2) If $f$ is smooth (locally of finite presentation and formally smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]), then $f'$ is smooth.

proof.text: *Separated and of finite type.* Since $f$ is proper it is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to $f$ and $g$, the base change $f':X'\to S'$ is separated and of finite type.

proof.text: *Universally closed.* Since $f$ is proper it is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-base-change], applied to $f$ and $g$, the base-change projection $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is universally closed.

proof.text: *Clause (1).* By the two preceding steps $f'$ is separated, of finite type and universally closed, i.e. proper by the definition [def-weil-proper-morphism].

*Locally of finite presentation.* Since $f$ is smooth it is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (the base change of a morphism locally of finite presentation along any morphism is locally of finite presentation), $f'$ is locally of finite presentation.

*Formally smooth.* Since $f$ is smooth it is formally smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Write $p:X'\to X$ for the first projection, so $f\circ p=g\circ f'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $i:T\to T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $S'$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with structure morphism $t':T'\to S'$ (so $T$ lies over $S'$ through $t'\circ i$), and let $a:T\to X'$ be a morphism over $S'$, i.e. $f'\circ a=t'\circ i$. (i) The same $i:T\to T'$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes over $S$, with structure morphism $g\circ t':T'\to S$: the closed immersion $i$, its ideal sheaf and the affineness of $T,T'$ do not involve the base, and $i$ is a morphism over $S$ since $(g\circ t')\circ i=g\circ(t'\circ i)$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. (ii) The morphism $p\circ a:T\to X$ is a morphism over $S$: $f\circ(p\circ a)=g\circ f'\circ a=(g\circ t')\circ i$. (iii) Since $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth], there is $b:T'\to X$ with $b\circ i=p\circ a$ and $f\circ b=g\circ t'$. (iv) As $f\circ b=g\circ t'$, the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a unique $a'=(b,t'):T'\to X'$ with $p\circ a'=b$ and $f'\circ a'=t'$; in particular $a'$ is a morphism over $S'$. (v) $a'\circ i=a$: both are morphisms $T\to X'$ with $p\circ(a'\circ i)=b\circ i=p\circ a$ and $f'\circ(a'\circ i)=t'\circ i=f'\circ a$, so they agree by the uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Hence every such lifting problem for $f'$ has a solution, i.e. $f'$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth].
